21: Written description: Board correctly found Bamberg's specification did not show possession of a white layer that melts below 220°C, so the copied claims lacked adequate written description support.

Because substantial evidence supports the Board's conclusion that Bamberg did not possess a white layer that melts below 220°C, Bamberg's specification fails to meet the written description requirement of 35 U.S.C. § 112.
663: Written description adequacy of PacBio's '551 provisional application for an embodiment of the interference count, so PacBio keeps the earlier filing date
We therefore affirm the Board's finding that the '551 application provides an adequate written description of at least one embodiment of the Count.
1191: Jury instruction that written description may be satisfied by disclosure of a newly characterized antigen was improper; remanded for amended instructions.
For those reasons, it was improper for the district court to instruct the jury as it did in the sentence at issue here.
1192: Denial of JMOL of no written description; Appellants not entitled to JMOL.
We therefore reject Appellants’ arguments and conclude that Appellants are not entitled to JMOL of no written description and no enablement.
1654: Written description for the TIBCO suit: the court held genuine issues of material fact exist on whether the specification shows possession of accessing disparate databases, reversing summary judgment of invalidity.
Accordingly, we reverse the district court's determination of summary judgment that the claims asserted against TIBCO are invalid for lack of written description support.
1755: Written description of claims 1, 2, 4 and 8 of the '601 patent; district court held claims invalid for lacking written description, Federal Circuit reversed because specification does not limit invention to patient-identifying sorting.
We agree with ScriptPro that the specification does not limit the claimed invention to sorting and storing prescription containers by patient-identifying information.
1807: Written description of the asserted claims; denial of JMOL that claims lack written description affirmed.
We see no error in the district court's denial of judgment as a matter of law that the asserted claims lack written description.
1843: Written description of the 'endorsement tag' and 'token' terms in the '516 patent claims
We therefore reverse the Board's conclusion that these claims are unpatentable as lacking adequate written description support.
1868: Written description of the '071 patent claims to daptomycin despite the structural diagram error; specification shows possession of the claimed compound.

We therefore uphold the district court's finding that the specification of the '071 patent contained the written description required by 35 U.S.C. § 112 and that the asserted claims are not invalid for lack of adequate written description.
1926: Written description adequacy for claims 10-15 of the '500 patent and all asserted claims of the '695 and '993 patents using terms selling computer, payment message, and authorization message
We see no error in the district court's conclusion that claims 10–15 of the '500 patent and all asserted claims of the '695 and '993 patents are invalid for lack of written description.
1966: Whether the tribunal properly rejected Dow's written description defense to the asserted claims; challenge rejected as ordinary legal error.
Dow challenges the tribunal's rejection of its written-description defense, J.A. 379–95, but its arguments amount to no more than allegations of ordinary legal error.
1990: Written description (35 U.S.C. 112 para. 1, pre-AIA): the specification lacks written description support for the challenged claims 1-28, so the claims are unpatentable.
We agree with the Board that the '022 specification lacks sufficient written description support for the challenged claims.
2020: Written description of the '320 patent: whether the specification as filed supports the claimed container with an integrated filter. Affirmed the Commission's holding that asserted claims 5-7, 18, and 20 lack written description support.
we affirm the Commission's conclusion that claims 5–7, 18, and 20 are invalid for lack of written description and that Solofill thus did not violate Section 337.
2081: Written description: whether the '072 application, through inherent disclosure of TBP-II, adequately describes the claimed protein of the '915 patent.
Therefore, the '072 application inherently discloses the remaining amino acids in the N-terminus sequence of TBP-II and serves as adequate written description support for the patent claiming TBP-II.
2172: Written description support in the Beachy priority applications ('076 and '964) for the interference Counts and the pending claims of the '121 and '934 applications.

To satisfy the written description requirement, the specification must sufficiently describe the claimed invention to a person skilled in the art and show that the inventor actually invented the claimed invention.
2338: Written description of negative claim limitation (CAS, RAS, bank address signals excluded); Board found specification provides reason to exclude and was supported by substantial evidence
We affirm the Board's finding, as supported by substantial evidence, that the "original '537 patent disclosure reasonably conveys a reason to exclude the relevant limitations."
2821: Written description support for claims 7, 9, and 13 of Mentor’s ’882 patent (‘independent’ signal routing clock); summary judgment of invalidity reversed because original claims show possession.
We reverse the grant of summary judgment that claims 7, 9, and 13 of the ’882 patent are invalid for lack of written description and remand for further proceedings.
2870: Written description of claimed separate IR and CR hydrocodone multiparticulates, each with inert beads, combined in a single dosage form; Board's finding of inadequate written description affirmed under substantial evidence review.

Although the written description generally discloses that a single dosage form may include both IR and CR hydrocodone components, it does not disclose a formulation wherein the IR and CR components exist as separate multiparticulates each containing an inert bead core.
2924: Written description for the equalization and discrete attenuation claims (56, 57, 76, 102, 103): the court held the specification does not support the claims, reversing the Board's finding of patentability.

Under the correct claim construction for the equalization and discrete attenuation claims, there is no substantial evidence in the record to support the Board's finding that claims 56, 57, 76, 102, and 103 of the '082 patent have sufficient written description support.
2925: Written description for the diverting element claims (38-41, 43-47, 49-50, 58-61, 75, 84-87, 89-93, 95-96, 104-107, 121): the court affirmed the Board's rejection because the specification does not show a diverting element inside the PLC.
Substantial evidence supports the Board's finding of lack of written description support for the diverting element claims.
2939: Written description of the '018 patent for random massively parallel sequencing; the Board relied on improper evidence and applied the wrong premise (whether the specification does not preclude targeted sequencing), so the court vacated and remanded without deciding adequacy.
For these reasons, we vacate the interference decisions and remand for the Board to reconsider whether Quake's relevant patents and applications satisfy the written description requirement.
2995: Written description support for substitute claims 47-50 under the flat-knit edge limitation; Board found adequate support and court affirmed.
we conclude that substantial evidence supports the Board’s decision that the proposed substitute claims are adequately supported by the written description of the ’011 patent.
3423: Written description: whether reissue claims 1-22 and 33-38 of the '162 patent, with the oxidizing and stabilizing step removed, meet the section 112 written description requirement; court held adequate.
We conclude that the CFC erred in holding reissue claims 1–22 and 33–38 invalid for failure to meet the written description requirement of section 112.
3502: Written description of Group II clinical profile claims ('353 and '118 patents): adequate written description found
We agree with Allergan that the specifications of the asserted patents provide an adequate written description of the invention claimed by the Group II claims.
3532: Written description for claim 41 of the '144 patent: long-term or permanent storage not covered, so no written description problem
Since the asserted claim does not cover long-term or permanent storage, the failure of the specification to describe such an embodiment presents no written description problem.
3582: Written description of the 'transitioning' limitation of claims 12-17 of the '901 application: adequate.
We therefore affirm the Board's finding that the '901 application contains an adequate written description of the "transitioning" limitation of claims 12–17.
3583: Written description of the 'minimizing the oxygen content' limitation of claims 7, 10 and 16 of the '901 application: adequate.
We therefore affirm the Board's decision that the '901 application contains an adequate written description of the "minimizing the oxygen content" limitation of claims 7, 10, and 16.
3765: Written description of claim 11 of the '195 patent: whether the specification shows possession of the claimed dissolution profile measured by USP 2 when the data were obtained using USP 1 (substantially equivalent methods).
we affirm the district court's conclusion.
3835: Written description support for the homogeneous matrix limitation
the district court did not err in finding that the 'homogeneous matrix' limitation was not indefinite and did not lack written description support.
3860: Written description: substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that the original specification of the '319 application does not provide sufficient written description support for the claimed suspended-fluoroquinolone composition.

Substantial evidence supports the Board's decision that the original specification of the '319 application does not provide sufficient written description support for the claimed suspended-fluoroquinolone composition.
3873: Written description of dissolution/release rate limitations; court held adequate written description.

The district court therefore did not err by concluding that the asserted claims of the '122 and '216 patents that recite the dissolution limitations are not invalid for inadequate written description.
3958: Written description: 'intangibles' not supported in original specification; new matter amendments improperly introduced
We agree with the Director that the claims lack adequate written description support.
4116: Written description of claims 206 and 220 of the '553 application: whether the specification shows possession of the simultaneous presentation of claimed features; court held lacking written description.
No reasonable factfinder could conclude that the '553 application meets the written description requirement.
4315: Whether the specification provides adequate written description for the claimed 12 mg/day or less dosage range for CYP2D6 poor metabolizers

We agree with Vanda that the district court did not clearly err in finding that the '610 patent contains adequate written description for the claimed '12 mg/day or less' dosage range for poor metabolizers.
4446: Written description: claims 65-67 of the '575 application lack written description support for the claimed concentration of about 6.6 x 10^11 particles per ml; Board's unpatentability finding affirmed.
For the foregoing reasons, we affirm the Board's finding that claims 65–67 are unpatentable for lack of sufficient written description.
4463: Written description for proposed claims 23-27 requiring solder pads configured to attach by a solder reflow process; the court held the specification inadequate under substantial evidence review.
Substantial evidence supports the PTAB’s determination that the specification does not provide adequate written description to allow a PHOSITA to recognize that the inventor invented what is claimed.
4592: Written description (§112(a)) of claims 1 and 4 reciting asenapine free base: the district court's finding of adequate written description was not clearly erroneous and was affirmed.
the district court did not clearly err in finding that Appellants had not established invalidity for lack of written description by clear and convincing evidence.
4676: Written description: the priority application disclosed and demonstrated possession of the full-length p75 sequence, and the district court's written description analysis for the claimed p75-IgG1 fusion protein was not clearly erroneous.
Accordingly, we conclude that the district court did not err in finding that the priority application disclosed and demonstrated possession of full-length p75.
4682: Written description of claims 1 and 35 of the '501 application under 35 U.S.C. §112(a); court held the claims lack written description.
We agree with the district court that the specification does not provide written description for the pending claims.
4684: Written description of the '597 patent for 2'-methyl-up 2'-fluoro-down nucleosides: majority held inadequate, reversing denial of JMOL

We reverse the district court's denial of judgment as a matter of law for failure to meet the written description requirement and hold that the '597 patent is invalid for lack of written description as well.
4709: Written description: the grandparent (original) application adequately supports the challenged claims, so they are entitled to its filing date.
A reasonable mind could understand this evidence to disclose to a skilled artisan a communications device according to the challenged claims.
4795: Written description: the Microspherix provisional adequately supports the challenged claims without strand-length limits under §112 ¶1 and §119(e).
This description adequately supports the claimed strand recited in Microspherix's patent claims.
4953: Written description (§112(a)) of the interference count: the '871 application does not adequately describe a method of treating MS with 480 mg/day of fumarates; Board's judgment that the claims lack written description affirmed under substantial evidence review.
Because substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that Forward's '871 application does not adequately disclose a method of treating MS with 480 mg of fumarates per day, we affirm.
5055: Written description (section 112(a)) for the call control patents ('052 and '561): specification found adequate to support claims covering IP technology.
we cannot conclude that Time Warner has shown by clear and convincing evidence that the call control specification lacks an adequate written description to support the asserted claims
5056: Written description (section 112(a)) for the broadband patents ('064, '084, '429): common specification incorporating call control specification found adequate.

we cannot agree, in light of the record at trial, that Time Warner has met its burden of showing by clear and convincing evidence that the common specification of the broadband patents lacks an adequate written description
5194: Written description (§112(a)): the '907 and '285 patents are invalid for failure to satisfy the written description requirement, as held in the companion opinion Nuvo Pharmaceuticals v. Dr. Reddy's Laboratories, 923 F.3d 1368 (Fed. Cir. 2019), and applied here to reverse the validity and infringement judgment.

In Nuvo Pharmaceuticals (Ireland) Designated Activity Company v. Dr. Reddy's Laboratories Inc., 923 F.3d 1368 (Fed. Cir. 2019), this court held that the '907 and '285 patents are invalid for failure to satisfy the written description requirement in 35 U.S.C. § 112(a).
5401: Claim 20 was not shown to lack adequate written description for the genus of more potent promoters.
6114: Written description support for claim 44 ('mode' limitation), including through incorporation by reference of the '479 patent; Board's finding of adequate support affirmed.
The Board correctly held that claim 44 is fully supported under 35 U.S.C. § 112 ¶ 1.
6445: Written description support for the copied count limitation in Wyoming's '425 patent and priority applications; Board found adequate written description, affirmed on the basis of the claim construction.
The Board did not err in its construction of the Count's "gradually and continuous changing" limitation. We therefore affirm the Board's judgment in the interference in favor of Wyoming.
6449: Written description of claim 4 of the '149 patent (genus of brimonidine/timolol combinations); found adequate.
The specification therefore discloses a representative—indeed, the sole—embodiment of the claimed genus
6610: Written description of claims 8 and 15 under §112(a): the Board's finding of adequate written description was affirmed.

Because substantial evidence supports the Board’s conclusion that the ’587 patent discloses that power is provided to the bus during the predetermined time when the drive is shut down, we are not persuaded that the Board’s determination should be overturned.
6776: Written description of the claimed therapeutic efficacy of uncoated PPI (efficacy written description issue); the court held the claims invalid as inadequately described.
Under those facts, the patent claims are invalid for lack of adequate written description pursuant to § 112, ¶ 1.
6794: Written description: the Board's finding that the shared specification does not adequately describe using random MPS to determine fetal aneuploidy was supported by substantial evidence, so the claims of the '018 patent and claim 25 of the '833 application are unpatentable.

In light of the limited disclosure value of the single Balasubramanian citation and the "about 30 bp of random sequence information are needed to identify a sequence" sentence, substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that those two items together are not adequate to convey using random MPS to determine fetal aneuploidy as claimed.
7096: Written description adequacy of the call control patents ('052 and '561) as to IP technology
we cannot conclude that Time Warner has shown by clear and convincing evidence that the call control specification lacks an adequate written description to support the asserted claims.
7097: Written description adequacy of the broadband patents ('064, '084, '429) as to IP technology

we cannot agree, in light of the record at trial, that Time Warner has met its burden of showing by clear and convincing evidence that the common specification of the broadband patents lacks an adequate written description
7221: Written description for reissue claims replacing 'thermoplastic' with 'plastic'. The Board applied a legal standard that ignored predictability and criticality, which conflicts with Ariad. The court vacated and remanded without deciding whether the written description requirement was satisfied.
We hold that the Board legally erred in its analysis of whether the '233 patent complies with the written description requirement under § 112, first paragraph.
7318: Written description: the 2009 Application lacks adequate written description for the washerless assemblies in the Asserted Claims, so those claims cannot claim its priority date.
we agree with the District Court that all Washerless Claims lack sufficient written description, meaning they cannot claim priority from the 2009 Application.
7319: Written description: the 2009 Application lacks adequate written description for the assemblies with a washer below the flashing (claim 8 of the 655 patent and claim 4 of the 339 patent), so those claims cannot claim its priority date.

we conclude that claim 8 of the '655 patent and claim 4 of the '339 patent lack sufficient written description in the 2009 Application, meaning they cannot claim priority from the 2009 Application and are therefore invalid.
7339: Whether the '534 provisional application provides written description support for the claimed HPMC/PEO formulations, so as to give the '376 patent an earlier priority date
the court finds that substantial evidence supports the Board's conclusion that the claims of the '376 patent do not have written description support in the '534 provisional application.
7426: Written description: claims at issue lack adequate written description support in the specification; Commission's invalidity finding affirmed under substantial evidence review.
We affirm on the written-description ground and do not reach anticipation or obviousness.
7495: Written description of claim 1 of the '880 patent (and shared '537 patent) is inadequate; summary judgment of invalidity affirmed.

We consequently conclude that the district court did not err in finding that no reasonable juror could find that the written description, including its various embodiments, supported all elements of claim 1 of the '880 patent.
7530: Written description of claim 2 of the '090 patent (method of treating R/R MCL at about 560 mg); district court found adequate support, affirmed.
we hold that the district court did not clearly err in finding that claim 2 of the '090 was adequately supported by the written description.
7535: Written description of claims 30 and 37 of the '857 patent (tablet formulations); found adequately described, affirmed.
That finding is not clearly erroneous, and we therefore affirm the district court's judgment with respect to claims 30 and 37 of the '857 patent.
7901: Written description for the negative no-loading-dose claim limitation added during prosecution; the court held the district court's finding of adequate written description was clearly erroneous and reversed the judgment that the claims were not invalid.
The district court's finding that the no-loading-dose limitation meets the written description requirement was clearly erroneous.
7903: Written description (§112(a)) for dependent claims 10 and 27 reciting a heating member length of about 75% to about 85%; Board found inadequate support, Federal Circuit held substantial evidence does not support that finding and vacated.

we find that substantial evidence does not support the Board's finding that claims 10 and 27 reciting a heating member "present on the heating projection along a segment having a length of about 75% to about 85% of a length of the disposable aerosol forming substance" lack written description support under § 112.
8075: Written description of the canola claims (claim 33 of '357, claim 5 of '579, claim 5 of '033); jury verdict of adequate written description affirmed.
Accordingly, we affirm the jury's verdict of written description as to the canola claims.
8076: Written description of the broader genus claims (claim 1 of '357, claims 2 and 10 of '880); jury verdict of adequate description reversed as unsupported.
We therefore reverse as to the broad genus claims.
8136: Written description support in the parent '629 application for the substitute claims with a side opening outside the rigid segment; Board found adequate support.
Medtronic has not demonstrated the Board's findings in this regard constitute legal error.
8296: Written description of the 'substantially horizontal bottom surface' limitation in the '833 patent. The district court held the claim invalid for inadequate written description on summary judgment; the Federal Circuit held a genuine issue of material fact remains and vacated.
a reasonable factfinder could conceivably find that a skilled artisan would understand that the specification discloses leg members with substantially horizontal bottom surfaces.
8367: Written description; summary judgment for Western Plastics affirmed because DuBose raised no genuine issue of material fact.
DuBose similarly argues the merits of inequitable conduct, written description, and indefiniteness without identifying a genuine issue of material fact warranting jury consideration.
8537: Written description (§112(a)) for the genus/subgenus claims of the ’830 patent as supported by the earlier NP2-P1 applications; no ipsis verbis disclosure and insufficient blaze marks
We conclude that the Board’s finding that NP2-P1 failed to provide sufficient blaze marks to support the ’830 patent’s priority claims was supported by substantial evidence.
8688: Written description support for the disputed determining limitation, measured by Agilent's originating specification; Board found adequate support and the court affirmed.
The Board did not err in concluding that Agilent's specification provided adequate written description support.
9239: Written description of claims 1-13 of the '273 patent and all claims of the '257 patent (court says claims 1-7 of '257); genus UGT claims lack adequate written description
we hold that claims 1-13 of the '273 patent and claims 1-7 of the '257 patent are invalid for lack of written description.
9379: Whether the challenged '084 and '431 claims are supported by written description in the common specification, so as to be entitled to the February 4, 2000 priority date; Board found no support.

We agree with Appellees that the Board's determination that "configured to periodically search via one or more networks to identify new web sites and to add the new web sites to the plurality of web sites" lacks written description support is supported by substantial evidence.
9443: Written description support for the substitute claim ('determining an intra mode for a neighboring block of a current block'); Board found no support and the court affirmed.

the Board's finding that the portions of the '849 patent specification that Ideahub identified in its motion to amend and subsequent revised motion to amend did not provide written description support for 'determining an intra mode for a neighboring block of a current block' is supported by substantial evidence
9501: Written description for claims 1, 7 and 12 (polymer weight percentage ranges) in the '571 application: not supported, so claims lack the 2009 priority date.
No range of 'about 40 wt % to about 60 wt %' appears in the '571 application.
9504: Written description for claim 8 (about 48.2 wt % polymer): supported by the '571 application, so claim 8 keeps the 2009 priority date.
we affirm the Board's decision that the '571 application provides written description support for claim 8
9695: Written description of the generic eyelet claim limitation in the '707 intervening application, which determines priority; court held substantial evidence supports the Board's finding of inadequate written description.
Substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that the '707 application lacks written description of flexible eyelets and, thus, the generic eyelet claim limitation.
10241: Written description of proposed substitute claims 23-25 of the '032 patent and 43-44 of the '380 patent; Board found adequate support; affirmed by reference to parallel decision.
We further reject Medtronic's arguments regarding lack of written description.
10403: Written description (§112(a)) for claims 3, 5, 9 and 11 of U.S. Patent No. 7,446,190 (scFv binding-element genus claims); court held the specification did not show possession of the full claimed genus, so the jury verdict of adequate written description lacked substantial evidence.
We hold that substantial evidence does not support the jury's finding of adequate written description for any of the asserted claims.
10702: Written description for the claimed 0.5 mg daily dosage limitation of the '405 patent; the court held the specification and priority application adequately describe it.

The Prophetic Trial and the EAE model provide sufficient written description to show that, as of the priority date, the inventors possessed a 0.5 daily fingolimod dosage as claimed in the '405 patent.
10703: Written description for the negative 'absent an immediately preceding loading dose' limitation; the court held it adequately described, rejecting a heightened standard for negative limitations.

we merely hold that, on this record, the district court did not clearly err in finding that a skilled artisan would read the '405 patent's disclosure to describe the 'absent an immediately preceding loading dose' negative limitation.
10730: Written description support in the GB Application for an internally-threaded piston rod in claims 21-30 of the '844 patent and substitute claims 31-38.
Based on the record before us, substantial evidence supports the Board's written description analysis for claims 21–30 and substitute claims 31–38.
10843: Written description support for the Procedural Selection Limitations in the proposed substitute claims; the Board found lack of written description and the court affirmed.

Because Mr. Fleming pointed to no passage in the specification that supports the aircraft activation requirements of the proposed amended claims, we conclude that substantial evidence supports the Board's finding of lack of written description
10939: Written description support for '793 patent claims as construed by the district court.
We also agree with United Therapeutics that the district court did not clearly err in finding that the claims of the '793 patent are supported by an adequate written description.
10974: Written description of claims 1-19 and substitute claims 21-39 (extension portion sized between two and three sheathing layers); Board found lack of written description and the court affirmed.
Accordingly, we affirm the unpatentability of claims 1–19 and substitute claims 21–39 for lack of written description.
11229: Written description (§112(a)) of claims 1-17 of the '961 patent; court held the specification does not show possession of PGGs as a gelling/aversive agent, so the claims are unpatentable.
The specification for the '961 patent does not provide adequate written description support, and neither does the '534 application.
11455: Written description (§112(a)) for Regents' P1 provisional application: whether P1 shows possession of Count 1 (single-RNA CRISPR-Cas9 functioning in eukaryotic cells). The court held the Board applied the correct standard and found P1 inadequate.
Contrary to Regents' arguments, the Board did not require P1 to convince a person of ordinary skill in the art of the success of Regents' invention.
11520: Written description (§112(a)): the asserted claims of the '179, '291, '792 and '516 patents, which do not require a glidant, were held adequately described; the district court's invalidity finding was reversed as clear error.

We therefore hold that the district court clearly erred in finding that the specification does not reasonably convey to a person of ordinary skill in the art that the inventors had possession of a formulation without a glidant
11648: Written description (§112(a)) for 'dedicated preamble' and 'index of the dedicated preamble' in the reissue claims; district court's denial of Samsung's JMOL of invalidity upheld as supported by substantial evidence.
Substantial evidence supports the jury's fact finding, and we agree the district court's denial of JMOL was appropriate.
11877: Written description of claims 1-6 and 23 as to filter media other than carbon block meeting the FRAP factor; Commission found inadequate written description; affirmed.
In sum, substantial evidence supports the Commission's determination that the asserted claims of the '141 patent lack adequate written description.
12103: Written description of claim 30 of the '270 patent (genus/subgenus of PGF analogs); court held no reasonable juror could find adequate written description, so claim 30 is invalid.

we conclude that no reasonable factfinder, taking the evidence in the light most favorable to Allergan, could have found anything other than clear and convincing evidence that claim 30 of the '270 patent is invalid for lack of adequate written description.
12272: Written description of genus claims to VHH antigen-binding proteins in application 16/282,082 (claims 77-83 and 85-94); Board found the specification lacks adequate written description support.

In view of the foregoing and because BAC does not challenge the Board's findings that the '082 application discloses only one VHH antigen-binding protein that meets each of the limitations claim of 77, and that the '082 application does not disclose a common structural feature for the claimed VHH antigen-binding proteins, we affirm the Board's determination that the '082 application lacks written description support.
12344: Written description of claims 1-4 of the '659 patent (valsartan and sacubitril administered in combination); district court found inadequate, Federal Circuit reversed and held adequate.
For those reasons, we hold that the district court clearly erred in finding that claims 1–4 of the ’659 patent are invalid for lack of written description.
12434: Written description: the asserted claims were held adequately described in the specification.
Therefore, again, we affirm the Commission’s finding that the asserted claims are not invalid for lack of adequate written description.
12450: Written description for the combined ranking step: substantial evidence supports Board finding of adequate written description.
we conclude that substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that the written description requirement of 35 U.S.C. § 112 was satisfied for the claimed 'combined ranking' step.
12485: Written description (§112(a)) challenge to claim 6 of the '650 patent
We thus reject Intuitive's written description challenge and decline to disturb the district court's judgment with respect to invalidity.
12545: Written description: whether the '938 utility application provides written description support for the six-by-five design claimed in the '345 design application. The Board's finding of no support was held supported by substantial evidence.
we affirm the Board's holding that the disclosure of the '938 application does not provide written description support for the design claimed in the '345 application.
12669: Written description under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) for asserted claims of the '439, '440 and '015 patents (crystalline cabozantinib (L)-malate salt genus); district court finding of adequate written description affirmed.
We affirm the district court's decision finding written description support pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) for the asserted claims of the '439, '440, and '015 patents.
12686: Written description of claim 30 of the '898 patent (compiling engine): held lacking written-description support under §112(a).
we conclude, as a matter of law, that claim 30 is invalid for lack of written-description support.
12703: Written description of the at least 98% native conformation limitation; the court found no substantial question of inadequate written description.
We see no material difference between Formycon's arguments and those presented by SB, which we have today held unpersuasive.
12713: Written description of negative limitation 'free of germanium' in continuation claims 1-15; Board's rejection affirmed as supported by substantial evidence and correct legal standard
Accordingly, we conclude that the Board applied the correct legal standard in affirming the examiner's rejection and that its final written decision is supported by substantial evidence.
12830: Written description adequacy of '802 patent claim limitation comparing hemolysis to a composition without magnesium; district court finding of adequate description upheld
On the merits, we hold that the district court did not clearly err in finding the '802 patent not invalid for lack of written description.
13149: Whether the '6839 Korean priority application provides written description support for the IAB limitation of claims 34-40 of the '653 patent; Board found it does not and court affirmed under substantial evidence review, so the patent is not entitled to the earlier priority date.
The Board's finding that the '653 patent lacks written description support for the IAB limitation was therefore supported by substantial evidence.
13222: Written description of humanized anti-CGRP antagonist antibody method claims; district court JMOL of no written description reversed, jury verdict reinstated
we conclude that JMOL of no written description was improper.
13393: Written description (§112(a)) for priority: whether the provisional's disclosure of C2-C12 alkyl supports the later claimed C1-C12 alkyl; court held it does not, and no genuine fact dispute exists.
We conclude that the '048 provisional does not convey to a skilled artisan that the inventors possessed —NHC(O)—C1-alkyl at the time of the '048 provisional's filing date.
13687: Written description support for substitute claims; original disclosure does not support new indicator generated in response to notification signal
We also conclude that the substitute claims are unsupported by the original disclosure
13692: Written description of the substitute claims' negative limitation ('without any communication' with the controller); specification found inadequate under substantial-evidence review.
Hence, substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that the specification fails to provide adequate written description support for the substitute claims and their negative limitation.
13846: Written description support for the negative limitation 'ambient air inlet excluding air passage through the first pipe section' in proposed substitute claims

we hold that substantial evidence supports the Board's finding that there is no "written description support for an inlet direct to ambient air and excluding air passage through the first pipe section."
14454: Written description of the amended 'type limitation' in claims 14 and 15 of the '180 patent; court held the jury's finding of adequate written description lacked substantial evidence and claims are invalid.
We hold that claims 14 and 15 of the '180 patent are invalid for lack of an adequate written description.
14519: Written description of the Gly/Phe-only tetrapeptide subgenus claims; 2004 application does not support priority
we conclude that substantial evidence does not support the jury's finding of adequate written description.
14748: Written description (§112(a)) for the glycosylation, upper bound (98%) and lower bound of the stability limitation of the '865 patent: the court held SB did not raise a substantial question of inadequate written description.
The district court did not clearly err in finding SB's challenge on this ground not to raise a substantial question.
14952: Written description for claim 9 (method of treating a patient with anti-C5 antibody): the specification does not show possession of treating a patient with the claimed Fc-modified antibody, so the written description was held inadequate.
Substantial evidence supports the ARP's determination that it does not.
14953: Written description for the Jepson claim 8: a Jepson preamble requires written description, and the applicant did not show that the claimed anti-C5 antibody genus was well-known in the art, so the written description was inadequate.
We agree with the ARP that a Jepson claim preamble requires written description.
15148: Written description: substantial evidence supports the finding that the '436 patent and '244 provisional lack written-description support for the register and bank address signal limitations of claim 16.
Substantial evidence supports the Board's findings that neither the '436 patent nor the '244 provisional contained written-description support for claim 16.
15157: Written description of overlapping zone scenes in the Zone Scene patents ('966 and '885); the district court's sua sponte invalidity ruling was reversed because the specification adequately conveys possession.

For at least the foregoing reasons, we hold that the district court erred in entering judgment that the asserted claims of the Zone Scene patents are invalid as lacking written description of overlapping zone scenes.
